stem: A data set consists of 10 numbers, including the numbers \(a\) and \(b\), and has a mean of 20. When \(a\) and \(b\) are both removed, the mean of the remaining 8 numbers is 18. When only \(a\) is removed, the mean of the remaining 9 numbers is 21. What is the value of \(b\)?
solution: The sum of all 10 numbers is \(10 \cdot 20 = 200\).
Without \(a\) and \(b\), the sum is \(8 \cdot 18 = 144\), so \(a + b = 200 - 144 = 56\).
Without only \(a\), the sum is \(9 \cdot 21 = 189\), so \(a = 200 - 189 = 11\).
verify:
a, b = symbols('a b')
sol = solve([Eq(200 - a - b, 8*18), Eq(200 - a, 9*21)], [a, b])
assert sol[a] == 11 and sol[b] == 45
assert [Rational(s) for s in spr_answers] == [45]
